comments.body: The original spec was not well-written in this regard, but imo the behavior the spec *should* define here is that the `animation-*` properties are not allowed inside of keyframes, but some related `animation-*` *descriptors* (with different, singular syntax) are allowed, and change the behavior of the keyframe itself.

That makes sense. Then, the spec would have descriptor definitions for the special `animation-timing-function` and `animation-composite` descriptors in addition to the property definitions they already have (like we have for `font-family`, property: https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts-4/#propdef-font-family, `@font-face` descriptor: https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts-4/#descdef-font-face-font-family. @tabatkins one question of bikeshed syntax I have is what is the correct `For` value for a case like this? ``` 
	Name: animation-timing-function
	Value: <>
	For: @keyframes
	Initial: N/A
``` Is `@keyframes` right even though these are always nested inside a specific sub-keyframe rule? Not sure it actually makes any difference, as it can be clear in prose where it is legal, but if there is existing precedent, would be good to follow it.

I think we can use @tabatkins's text as the proposal (*with small edits by me):

Fix spec to say `animation-*` properties are not allowed inside of keyframes, but some related `animation-*` descriptors with singular syntax are allowed, and change the behavior of the keyframe itself.

The CSSWG will automatically accept this resolution one week from now if no objections are raised here. Anyone can add an emoji to this comment to express support. If you do not support this resolution, please add a new comment.

Proposed Resolution: Define `animation-*` descriptors with syntax subsets for use in `@keyframes`

I agree with the discussion here, but the proposed resolution is very vague. Let's go with ydaniv's wording. :)

Proposed Resolution: Fix spec to say `animation-*` properties are not allowed inside of keyframes, but corresponding `animation-*` descriptors with singular syntax are allowed, and change the behavior of the keyframe itself.
I try to come up with a proposed async resolution that fits into an email subject line. I did add more details in the body of the www-style email and linked back here.

I have two minor concerns about defining these `animation-*` properties accepted in keyframe rules, as descriptors for `@keyframes`.

(1) This should be updated ([CSS Syntax](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-syntax-3/#css-descriptor-declarations)):

  > Declarations are further categorized as property declarations or descriptor declarations, with the former setting CSS properties and appearing most often in qualified rules and the latter setting CSS descriptors, which appear only in at-rules.

Perhaps property declarations apply to elements, while descriptor declarations apply to the resource represented by the rule?

(2) And I think any author would expect `@keyframes { animation-timing-function: ease }` to be valid, given this:

  > **Name:** `animation-timing-function`
  > **For:** `@keyframes`

If `For` is merely a namespacing mechanisme, I do not see the point of exposing it.

> (2) And I think any author would expect `@keyframes { animation-timing-function: ease }` to be valid, given this:
> 
> > **Name:** `animation-timing-function`
> > **For:** `@keyframes`
> 
> If `For` is merely a namespacing mechanisme, I do not see the point of exposing it.

Alternatively, we could add a definition for nested scope and use that. For example, we could have something like this text somewhere:

"`@keyframes` rules use a nested scope for each individual keyframe. Though they are not introduced with an `@` name, they are referenced in this specification as "{some-name-for-the-individual-keyframe-scope}"."
